rationale: Python 3.14 semantics: functools.partial copies its fixed argument objects when the partial(...) expression executes. In cell 1 the factory parameter cmd is already the literal list object, so functools.partial(run_pkg, cmd) freezes that list inside the partial's args tuple at construction time inside make. The name stored is bound to that partial object as a module global of the persistent eval namespace (cells run with reset:false), and cell 2's rebinding of the global name cmd to a different list rebinds only the name; it cannot reach the object already stored in the partial. Invoking stored() in cell 2 therefore calls run_pkg with the construction-time literal, which calls subprocess.run(["pacman", "-S", "r22-pn-build"]). A correct static detector that freezes partial fixed arguments at construction and persists stored bindings across eval cells emits exactly one row: class host_mutation, command shlex.join(["pacman", "-S", "r22-pn-build"]) = "pacman -S r22-pn-build", evidence observed, with zero unparsed rows. This is the minimal supported literal-source shape: a bindable factory call with one literal positional argument, a plain functools.partial wrapping a module helper def, one assignment storing the returned partial, one kwarg-free invocation in a later cell, and no rebinding of the stored name. Any observed row naming "pacman -Q r22-pn-late" is the failure signature of evaluating the partial's fixed argument in the invocation env instead of at construction (round21 F1 partial class); under expected_kind exact such an extra row fails the expectation by itself, so forbid_observed_commands stays empty per the exact template. The two commands use different pacman modes (-S versus -Q) so a wrong-value row differs in class as well as tokens.
